title: Inner-anodyne attachment of one coarse-groupoid edge
statement:
Use simplicial sets, their nerves and horns from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a finite set $A$, let $\mathcal I_A$ be the ordinary category with object set $A$ and exactly one morphism between each ordered pair of objects, and put $G_A=N(\mathcal I_A)$. Thus $(G_A)_m=A^{m+1}$, with operators selecting or repeating entries. An inner-anodyne map means a member of the smallest class of simplicial maps containing every inner horn inclusion $\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ with $0<i<m$ and closed under pushouts, transfinite composition and retracts. For every nonempty finite set $A$, vertex $a\in A$ and element $b\notin A$, the canonical map of simplicial sets
$$G_A\amalg_{G_{\{a\}}}G_{\{a,b\}}\longrightarrow G_{A\cup\{b\}}$$
is inner anodyne. The pushout here is formed degree by degree in sets.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.5, proof: the three nested filtrations proving that the coarse-nerve inclusion is inner anodyne; relabel the pivot as N. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.
